about: Reproduction of the seed paper's figures (NHB 2026, national influence) from its own published data, through figpipe.grammar intents.

reproduction_layers.L0 data construction: NOT reproduced. The authors built the tables from a ~240M-work OpenAlex snapshot via AWS Athena SQL, four key-phrase extractors and a 10-year citation window. This work starts from the published OUTPUT_* aggregates and the authors' own 10,046-term censored list, so an error in that construction would be INHERITED, not detected.
reproduction_layers.L1 transformation: Reproduced. The R recipe was re-implemented in Python: sum weights per dyad-year, filter to the censored terms, outer-join the two networks, per-year z-scoring, relative influence as the difference, per-country centrality, Gini, mean +/- s.e.m. This is a re-implementation of the SAME formulas, not an independent derivation: where the authors' code is wrong, the reproduction is wrong the same way.
reproduction_layers.L2 figures: Partially reproduced: 13 of the paper's 18 panels (Fig 1a/1b 2, Fig 3a/b/c 3, Fig 5 4, Fig 7 4). Fig 2 (QAP permutations) is not in the package; Fig 4 was omitted (same construction as Fig 3); Fig 6 needs a country->region mapping the package does not ship.
reproduction_layers.L3 typography: Deliberately different. The originals are ggplot2 figures rendered by the journal (8x8 in, ~9-10 pt, grey grid, red/green diverging); the reproductions follow Nature's submission spec (183 mm, 5-7 pt, Okabe-Ito, red-blue diverging). The statistics agree; the graphic language does not, and must not be read as fidelity.

Fig 2.why: QAP regression coefficients and permutation outputs are not in the published data package

Fig 4.why: same construction as Fig 3 from relative influence; omitted to keep the run short -- the derived tables already support it

Fig 6.why: arc diagram and region matrix need a country->region mapping the seed does not include (the R recipe uses raster::ccodes + a custom UNREGION1 table)

discrepancies.statistic: Pearson r, term papers vs attributional papers
discrepancies.resolution: UNRESOLVED: published 0.78 matches the log-scale value and the axes are log10, but the authors' ggpubr::stat_cor call reads as raw-scale. Both values are reported; the figure quotes the drawn scale.
discrepancies.risk: if the authors computed raw-scale r, then 0.78 and 0.775 agree by coincidence and the gap is real

figures.estimator: Fig 1a: share of unique (term, year, influencer) rows per country; Fig 1b: Pearson r on log10(n_papers), log10(n_cites)
deviations: Fig 1b shows marginal histograms on BOTH axes in the paper; the reproduction has the top marginal only, because the right side is used by the colour bar.
Fig 1a country names come from a small vendored ISO2 table; the authors use raster::ccodes(), which is not in the package.
Fig 1b annotation quotes the log-scale r (0.775) to match the drawn scale; the raw-scale r is 0.83. See the Fig 1b discrepancy record.

figures.estimator: Pearson r of yearly Gini / yearly mean centrality against year
deviations: The paper letters panel c once and splits it into two facets; the reproduction uses letters c and d, so it carries one more letter.
Published facets use free_y; the reproduction shares one y scale per network.
The published panels carry a light grey grid; the reproduction has no gridlines (figpipe style rule).

figures.estimator: Pearson r of yearly mean relative influence against year, per core/periphery dyad class
deviations: Pane titles shortened from three lines to one.
The loess band is APPROXIMATED (tricube local linear, global residual variance); it is not ggplot2's loess variance -- stated in drawlib.
Directional labels ('greater discursive/attributational influence') are placed by eye from the published figure, not measured.

figures.estimator: Pearson r of yearly mean cosine similarity against year, n=19 (1995-2013)
deviations: Pane titles shortened from three lines to one.
Marker and fit colours matched to the published panel (black points, blue fit).

self_check.note: counts are derived from the agreement tree, never typed by hand
